youtube.title: GRANT DIXON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with documentary maker Grant Dixon about his analysis of a University of Otago study showing childhood autism diagnoses have more than trippled over 15 years. Dixon argues the researchers overlooked a strong correlation with rising antigen exposure from the vaccination schedule, and discusses falling MMR uptake among Māori families, racial differences in vaccine susceptibility, and his concerns about compounding health risks from an expanding vaccine schedule. Editorial Note: The figure quoted in this interview that autism has risen by 340% is incorrect. It is 240%, not 340% , when describing the actual increase. The original amount represents 100%. If something grows to 3.4 times its original size, it is now 340% of the original amount . However, the increase itself is calculated by subtracting the original 100% from the new 340%, giving a 240% increase . youtube.title: JODIE BRUNING
youtube.summary: In this interview, sociologist Jodie Bruning raises concerns about the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s growing role in modernising the country’s retail payment system, arguing that the shift toward real-time payments could create infrastructure capable of supporting future central bank digital currencies or be linked with other government services and personal data. Bruning questions whether decisions involving critical digital infrastructure should be made by the RBNZ rather than Parliament, and calls for a new legislative framework with stronger democratic oversight.
